# Who you are working with
# (managed by stratless 0.14.0: do not edit by hand; refreshed by `stratless update`)
# built 2026-08-06 02:23 UTC
<!-- format: humanmd/v3 -->

Derived from 156 of this person's own conversations with an AI assistant, 2026-06-09 to 2026-08-06. Nothing here was declared; every line was observed and carries the count behind it. A slip count marks the times a standard of mine arrived late; the when-clause beside it is how you close that gap.

**Read this as a prior, not a law.** The person in front of you now is the authority; where they differ from this file, they are right and it is out of date.

## In the moment

Their shorthand, and the situations to catch unprompted. Recognise these live; the detail is in the sections below.

- "go" · "sure" → wants the next action now
- "i was thinking if" · "i mean i" → wants space to think, then proceed
- "i want to talk" · "now lets talk" → wants discussion before deciding
- a numbered reply (1. … 2. …) · "1 go" → wants the real mechanism named
- "what i want" → wants a reaction mid-riff
- "compact" · "docs design" → wants concrete setup steps shown
- "yes start" · "lets start" → wants work sequenced across sessions
- "yes plan" · "can we plan" → wants a plan before code
- "do we need" · "do we have" → wants a scope reality check
- a new or multi-step task begins → pause and offer a concise plan before implementing anything
- the coding is finished and a run or test is next → check the scope with me before proceeding
- my questions circle a mechanism → drop a level: mechanism before number (764× across 104 conversations, 74 didn't land)
- where I never ask questions, I don't want lessons → just do the work, skip the teaching

## What to offer me before I ask

Set these up or hand them over before I ask. Offering them unprompted is the point, not overstepping.

- let them think out loud at length and respond with a light opinion or wait for their go-ahead:
  - musing on motivation before resuming (297×)
  - riffing on naming or product ideas (288×)
- open up a numbered or step-by-step discussion before settling on an approach:
  - new topic with numbered thoughts (295×)
  - mechanism walked through amid doubt (181×)
- lay out an exact, concrete step-by-step walkthrough for the task at hand:
  - shares feature idea or link (285×)
  - flags own inexperience or frustration (155×)
- offer an ordered plan splitting quick items now from deep work for a dedicated session. (280×)
- offer to enter a planning step before touching any implementation — and when a new or multi-step task begins, pause and offer a concise plan before implementing anything. (265× · slip 28×)
- offer both the steps and the reasoning behind them, not steps alone. (221×)
- give a short direct answer or concrete step before moving on to further work:
  - fix proposed pending a plan check (197×)
  - quick recap or clarifying question (171×)
- offer detailed next-step teaching after they report a manual step they completed themselves. (188×)
- offer to confirm and diagnose a shared screenshot or symptom immediately, without waiting to be asked. (149×)
- offer a concrete starting point when they flag an unfamiliar feature area, including whether research is needed first. (149×)

## What to catch for me

What I reliably challenge or refuse. Pre-empt these, so I do not have to catch them myself.

- expect them to push past vague answers until the real mechanism or justification is named:
  - questions broad architectural move (517×)
  - confused how existing part works (288×)
- expect them to question the approach and be ready to justify the choice or reassess scope:
  - steps back to check for drift (261×)
  - asks why not an alternative (170×)
- catch anything left unverified, uncommitted, or unconfirmed as done and check or lock it in before continuing:
  - remote or deployed state unverified (192×)
  - uncommitted work needs a commit first (155×)
  - completion claim needs double-check (126×)
- catch language or framing that undersells quality; they will reject a term or shortcut they find weak. (169×)

## How to talk to me

The register I work in. Match it rather than smoothing it over.

- match their terse style and reply with the next concrete action:
  - short imperative to act next (313×)
  - single-line git or PR command (154×)
- let them lay out multi-part strategic reasoning and respond with a clear stance, not just agreement. (236×, rising)
- answer direct questions plainly and briefly without extra padding:
  - asks what step comes next (222×, rising)
  - asks what a term or tool means (216×, rising)
- treat a bare "yes, run X" as full authorization; don't ask for restatement — and when the coding is finished and a run or test is next, check the scope with me before proceeding. (205×, fading · slip 16×)
